definitions.gloss: new school term; new semester; new academic term
definitions.explanation: The beginning of a new academic term or semester. In Japan, the school year traditionally starts in April, so 新学期 most commonly refers to the start of the April term.

examples.japanese: {新学期|しんがっき}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The new school term has begun.

examples.japanese: {新学期|しんがっき}に{向|む}けて{教科書|きょうかしょ}を{買|か}いそろえた。
examples.english: I bought all the textbooks in preparation for the new term.

examples.japanese: {新学期|しんがっき}になると、{新|あたら}しい{友達|ともだち}ができるのが{楽|たの}しみだ。
examples.english: When the new term starts, I look forward to making new friends.

notes:
USAGE:
{新学期|しんがっき} combines {新|しん} (new) and {学期|がっき} (school term/semester). In Japan, the academic year begins in April, so {新学期|しんがっき} most often refers to the spring term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新学期|しんがっき}が{始|はじ}まる (the new term begins)
- {新学期|しんがっき}に{向|む}けて (in preparation for the new term)
- {新学期|しんがっき}の{準備|じゅんび} (preparation for the new term)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{学期|がっき} is the general word for a school term or semester. {新年度|しんねんど} refers to the new fiscal or academic year as a whole, which is broader than a single term.
